scope: LOGIN SYSTEM FULL ROOT CAUSE AUDIT + ONE-SHOT FIX

constraints_honored.changed_area: auth flow, session transport, frontend auth state

primary_root_cause.summary: The frontend treated the login response session_token as authenticated state, but subsequent API authentication still depended on cookie propagation through the browser and Next proxy. When the cookie was missing, stale, blocked by SameSite/Secure/Path behavior, or not forwarded, the backend returned 401 even though the frontend had a valid login token.
primary_root_cause.responsible_layer: shared auth session boundary: frontend API client/proxy and backend session resolver

secondary_causes.summary: Login did not consistently expose a complete ready-to-use auth state to the frontend: user.id, user.role, user.organization_id, session_token, and auth_complete=true.
/auth/me was used as a login confirmation path. A slow or failed /auth/me request could override a successful login and show Unable to sign in.
401 responses from /auth/login and /auth/me could trigger global unauthenticated state transitions instead of being treated as local login or supplemental hydration failures.
Login previously included side effects in the synchronous response path, including audit and login bookkeeping writes, increasing timeout risk under load.
Capability bootstrap caching was keyed by cookie only, so token-only sessions could collapse into an anonymous cache key.

frontend_login_flow.login_form_submit: Single-submit guard is present; overlapping login submissions are blocked.
frontend_login_flow.auth_provider_state_transition: Login response now sets authenticated state directly. Background hydration is supplemental.
frontend_login_flow.token_storage: session_token is persisted with authComplete=true and user identity in localStorage.
frontend_login_flow.redirect_logic: Successful login redirects immediately to dashboard or force-password-reset.
frontend_login_flow.risk_before_fix: Valid login could be replaced by /auth/me failure or global unauthorized handling.

backend_login_api.hot_path: Password verify, user lookup, lightweight session creation, response.
backend_login_api.response_contract: Returns user.id, user.role, user.organization_id, session_token, auth_complete=true.
backend_login_api.deferred_work: Login success/failure side effects are queued outside the response path.
backend_login_api.risk_before_fix: Synchronous side effects increased timeout exposure.

session_cookie_mechanism.token_policy: X-Session-Token is now a first-class session transport and is resolved before cookie fallback.
session_cookie_mechanism.proxy_forwarding: Next backend proxy forwards X-Session-Token to FastAPI.

auth_me_behavior.failure_effect: Does not clear authenticated state when a valid login snapshot already exists.

api_failure_paths.auth_failure_401: Login form treats 401 from /auth/login as invalid credentials.
api_failure_paths.timeout_or_backend_failure: Login form shows service unavailable instead of invalid credentials.

root_cause_decision.frontend_responsibility: The API client did not consistently attach the login response session_token to subsequent requests, and auth state could rely on /auth/me hydration.
root_cause_decision.backend_responsibility: Auth dependencies and middlewares read only the session cookie, so a valid session_token from login could not authenticate follow-up requests.
